description: SN time dilation test using fitted TEP model parameters

literature_context: Goldhaber et al. 2001 (ApJ 558, 359): Direct time dilation from SN light curves
Blondin et al. 2008 (A&A 477, 717): Time dilation constraints from SN spectral features
Foley et al. 2018 (ApJS 237, 26): Pantheon+ methodology and stretch parameter usage
Betoule et al. 2014 (A&A 568, A22): SALT2 model and stretch parameter interpretation
diagnostic_status.not_a_claim: This is NOT a time-dilation proof; it tests internal consistency of TEP framework
diagnostic_status.path_to_publication_grade: For definitive time-dilation test: use compressed likelihood from Blondin et al. 2008 (A&A 477, 717) or similar, or implement full light-curve modeling with TEP-modified bolometric corrections.

proxy_justification.caveat: SALT2 x1 is degenerate with intrinsic brightness and color; not a direct time-dilation measurement
proxy_justification.theoretical_basis: TEP predicts that temporal shear (Sigma) affects photon propagation timescales; SALT2 x1 captures observed light-curve width variations

interpretation: Internal consistency check - SALT2 x1 as diagnostic proxy for temporal shear effects
key_finding: Diagnostic consistency: SALT2 x1 correlates with TEP path enhancement

notes: Step 023 serves as diagnostic consistency check within TEP framework
SALT2 x1 correlation with Sigma_eff validates internal model consistency
For definitive time-dilation claims, see future step implementing compressed likelihood from Blondin et al.
